newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia demands swift release of Tajik hostages.
newsitem.headline: Russia demands swift release of Tajik hostages.

text.p: Russian deputy prime minister Vitaly Ignatyenko demanded on Sunday that Tajik rebels release 11 Russian and Western hostages they are still holding in defiance of a pledge they gave to the Tajik government.

"Either you begin to release the hostages now or you bear the full responsibility (for the consequences)," Itar-Tass news agency quoted Ignatyenko as telling rebel leader Bakhrom Sadirov by telephone from Moscow.
"Be a man, fulfil the promises you made, release the hostages, do not play with human lives," he said.

On Saturday the Tajik authorities, backed by Moscow, handed over more than 30 fighters to Sadirov on the understanding that he would in return release his 11 captives, who include Russian journalists, United Nations military observers and Tajik Security Minister Saidamir Zukhurov.

But the rebels, based on top of a mountain in a remote rocky region 80 km (50 miles) from the Tajik capital Dushanbe, failed to free the hostages and broke off walkie-talkie negotiations until Sunday morning.

Russian diplomat Gennady Sizov, who is based in Tajikistan, has resumed direct negotiations with the rebels, Ignatyenko told Tass. In their telephone conversation, Ignatyenko and Sadirov agreed to stay in regular contact, Tass said.
Interfax news agency reported Sadirov as saying he had no intention of leaving the mountains with his hostages.
A Tajik government helicopter flew over the mountain base early this morning to reconnoitre the scene.
The Tajik government has said it might try to use force to free the hostages though a deadline of 1030 local time (0530 GMT) passed without incident.

The hostage crisis started on February 4, when Bakhrom Sadirov seized hostages and demanded that the government allow free passage for his brother Rizvon and some 40 of his men to his base in Tajikistan from neighbouring Afghanistan.
